stateDescription: Entering the field of experience begins a life of relationship, limitation and possibility.
An appearance is taken to be the whole reality rather than one way it is being encountered.
A frustrated desire or threatened boundary gathers energy into opposition.
The wish to acquire continues after a practical need has been met.
Life is encountered through a body, a place and the material conditions that sustain them.
Attachment to a desired view of events interferes with recognising what is happening.
An image of personal importance becomes something that must continually be defended.
Fear of having less makes sharing or another person’s gain feel threatening.
Desire draws attention toward experiences that promise pleasure or relief.
A chosen discipline reduces what obscures attention and conduct.
Music, play and sensory pleasure can restore a mind narrowed by effort.
Another person's good fortune brings an unacknowledged wish into view.
A familiar role falls quiet before a new direction has become clear.
The mind gives shape to possibilities that are not yet present.
An imagined outcome becomes more compelling than the circumstances in front of you.
Dislike hardens into a demand that a person or experience disappear.
Another being's vulnerability interrupts the habit of judging solely by performance.
Gladness arises when attention is available to what is already sustaining life.
Intentions enter the world through actions and acquire consequences beyond your control.
Something held as exclusively yours becomes available to another.
Acknowledging harm opens the possibility of changing what happens next.
A decision is considered in relation to commitments, circumstances and the wellbeing of others.
Conditions briefly support a sense of harmony and sufficiency.
A surrounding group makes an unhelpful habit easier to repeat.
Good company strengthens the capacity to act with care and honesty.
A loss or disappointment asks to be acknowledged rather than argued away.
Action is offered for a purpose larger than personal credit.
A responsibility begins to fit your capacities and circumstances.
Convenience or allegiance draws conduct away from a responsibility you recognise.
Repeated small choices make a constructive response easier to reach.
Something is encountered as worthy of attention beyond its usefulness to you.
Competing demands are brought into a workable relationship.
A small sensory impression carries a memory or changes the atmosphere of experience.
Experience is received with its particular flavour instead of being reduced to a judgment of success or failure.
An avoided consequence becomes difficult to ignore.
Attention becomes less clouded by the need to defend a preferred story.
Information becomes understanding when it changes how you meet experience.
The felt capacity to participate returns through attention to ordinary sources of energy.
What has completed its purpose is allowed to leave.
Resources and attention move through a larger network of relationships.
Your concern is recognised as one expression of a wider human condition.
Intensity can illuminate a commitment or consume the conditions needed to sustain it.
The capacity to reflect gives you a choice within circumstances you did not choose.
A partial account of experience is mistaken for the whole.
Careful inquiry replaces the comfort of an untested answer.
A lasting commitment is distinguished from a passing impulse.
Attention listens without immediately converting experience into action or argument.
The active side of experience seeks a clear direction and an appropriate limit.
The receptive side of experience allows impressions to arrive before deciding what to do.
Attention gathers around a chosen practice instead of following every competing demand.
The question returns to material conditions: body, place, time and resources.
Force seeks to overcome resistance without adequate regard for what is injured.
A response finds a workable form without losing contact with its purpose.
Care becomes a sustained orientation rather than a passing mood.
A useful sense of self contracts into the requirement that every event affirm it.
A sound or repeated phrase gathers scattered attention into a shared rhythm.
Change becomes noticeable through movement, contact and the exchange of ideas.
Understanding makes a situation more visible and can help others find their bearings.
Speech and conduct are brought closer to what you actually know and intend.
Intelligence considers both immediate effects and the larger purpose of an action.
Reasoning is used to defend an impulse after the decision has effectively been made.
Wellbeing is experienced as something more stable than the satisfaction of a single demand.
Confusion, avoidance or exhaustion reduces the capacity to see and respond.
Experience is seen within the changing conditions that make it possible.
Awareness can hold a thought or feeling without immediately following it.
Contentment is approached without making possession or achievement its condition.
An established form loses its usefulness and makes room for a different arrangement.
The self is contemplated as participating in a reality larger than its private concerns.
A new arrangement begins to take form from conditions already present.
Clarity, steadiness and care support a less reactive response.
Desire and effort set experience in motion and seek a result.
Habit continues because changing it seems harder than enduring its cost.
